examples.title: A missed check-in is not a motive

scenarioFrame.context: A fictional service dashboard records two missed check-ins during one week.
availableSignals: The dashboard records two missed check-ins.
A fictional participant reports feeling overwhelmed.
An analyst proposes disengagement as an explanation.
scenarioFrame.illustration: The dashboard entry is an observation, the participant statement is a report, and disengagement is an inference that remains unverified.
scenarioFrame.learnerPrompt: Classify each signal and state which source boundary must remain attached.
scenarioFrame.boundaryReminder: Do not promote the analyst's explanation into an observed fact.

scenarioFrame.context: A fictional product records a demand drop during a single week.
availableSignals: Weekly demand is lower than the prior week.
A team member says the market rejected the product.
No seasonal or channel data is available.
scenarioFrame.illustration: The observed drop supports a time-bounded change claim but not a complete causal explanation.
scenarioFrame.learnerPrompt: Rewrite the reading so its time range, alternatives and unknowns remain visible.
scenarioFrame.boundaryReminder: Do not turn a fluent causal story into a diagnosis or certainty claim.

scenarioFrame.context: A fictional household wants to reduce a monthly service cost while a fixed-term contract remains active.
availableSignals: The stated goal is a lower monthly cost.
The current contract has an early-exit condition.
scenarioFrame.illustration: Navigation maps the goal, options and exit constraint without selecting a configuration for the household.
scenarioFrame.learnerPrompt: State the current position, map the options and identify who retains the decision.
scenarioFrame.boundaryReminder: Option mapping is not action selection or professional advice.

scenarioFrame.context: A fictional team changes a workflow and reviews the result after two weeks.
availableSignals: The relationship between the workflow change and both outcomes is not fully known.
scenarioFrame.illustration: Review links the action and outcomes while preserving the mixed result, uncertainty and next review point.
scenarioFrame.learnerPrompt: Describe the continuation state without treating either outcome as complete proof.
scenarioFrame.boundaryReminder: Do not erase prior lineage or unresolved causes when forming the next state.

examples.title: Learning completion is not assignment authority

scenarioFrame.context: A fictional facilitator completes an academy learning sequence but has no verified credential, service entitlement or accepted assignment.
availableSignals: Entitlement and assignment responsibility are unresolved.
scenarioFrame.illustration: Learning completion, capability review, credential evidence, entitlement and professional assignment remain separate governed states.
scenarioFrame.learnerPrompt: Classify the five states and identify which gates remain unresolved.
scenarioFrame.boundaryReminder: Academy content cannot grant a credential, entitlement, assignment or professional authority.
